diagram_candidates.claim: For d in {2,3}, recursively select the lower median hyperplane in every coordinate of side length at least two, remove their union as a separator, recursively order up to 2^d child boxes, then append separator vertices lexicographically.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The item explicitly defines coordinate grids and a recursive geometric separator ordering. A small 2D grid and its first split can show how the separator leaves four child boxes; a second level or companion recursion tree would explain the order clearly.
diagram_candidates.specific_content: Draw a small square grid with the selected lower-median row and column highlighted as S, label the at most four nonempty child boxes, and show that child boxes are ordered by lower corners before separator vertices are appended lexicographically. Do not imply a fill or complexity bound; the source explicitly makes neither claim.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_check: The median coordinate is floor((m-1)/2) positions below in a side of length m; the separator is the union of selected coordinate hyperplanes and the children are the remaining rectangular boxes. The candidate must preserve the source lexicographic order and make no claim about arbitrary graphs.

diagram_mathematics_checks: No existing TikZ or other mathematical diagrams were present in the assigned screenshots (receipt tikz_count is zero throughout); therefore there were no existing diagram labels, maps, domains/codomains, signs, orientations, indices, or combinatorics to validate. The nested-dissection candidate is optional editorial explanation, not a defect.
other_checks: The other assigned titles and complete ItemBody renders showed no confirmed broken TeX/KaTeX or TikZ output. Punctuation and reference-link wrapping were not classified as defects. Apparent edge truncation was not recorded without an unambiguous standalone-tile clipping confirmation.
